Efforts to improve diplomatic relations with Cuba and eliminate the U.S. trade embargo with the communist island nation have ramped up since President Obama's executive order announcement in December last year. The next round in administrative negotiations to restore diplomatic ties with Cuba is this Friday in Washington. The congressional effort to end the embargo and normalize relations with Cuba has now begun on Capitol Hill. Minnesota U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar introduced the Freedom to Export to Cuba Act with co-sponsors of the legislation on both sides of the aisle. But Senator Klobuchar says the legislation supports policy changes that can improve the lives of the Cuban people. Senator Klobuchar says the Cuban people want a closer relationship with the U.S. and she says the time is right to approve legislation to bring about that change.

transcript: I think part of this is there has been some changes in Cuba. There's been a promotion of the private sector. There's now 500,000 people working in the private sector, whether it seems just businesses in their homes or a taxi service. Secondly, there are now in the midst of developing a huge new port, and we were some of the first members of Congress to be able to see it. Senator Warner, Senator McCaskill and myself. It is a big improvement on the Havana port, which we use mainly for tourism. But this port is going to be able to take in big ships and the kind of ships now we're seeing in international shipping and the kind of ships that can be loaded with American agricultural products. And so those two examples, and I think you've just seen some changes in their leadership in terms of the messages they're sending. One of the things that I was struck by when I was there, and one of the reasons that I put forward the bipartisan bill to list the embargo, is that Cubans want to work with Americans. They were so excited about it. They like Americans, unlike some of the countries that we do business with sometimes. I just think there's a lot of promise and the final thing I'd say is having met with the ambassadors from Norway and Spain and Germany, all of whom Sweden have Brazil have relations with Cuba. Those countries are starting to move now and if we don't get our act together and are able to lift this embargo and start trading more of our agricultural products, we're going to lose out on the market. Canada already does hundreds of millions of dollars at this and that's not what is going to happen for us unless we start working on lifting the embargo.
